issues.issue: The deductible is "as specified in G. 3. a. and G. 3. b. on the DECLARATIONS, Form RM1000, or on the ADDITIONAL DEDUCTIBLES AND WAITING PERIODS, Form RM1115," but those Declarations items read "$Not Applicable" (c022, c023). The cross-reference points to blanks, leaving the applicable deductible to be found elsewhere.
The time deductible is "a time period of Not Applicable immediately following the loss," which is not a period at all. Whether that means no time deductible or an inoperable condition is left open.

This makes asterisked deductibles cumulative, while DECLARATIONS G. (c027) and Form RM1115 B. (c315) say no more than the largest applicable deductible will be used. Whether deductibles stack in a service-interruption loss requires reconciling these.

The Schedule covers "All covered locations except as indicated in B., C., and D. below," but items B., C. and D. are left blank, so the exception refers to nothing. The $250,000 figure is also printed without identifying whether it is a limit or a deductible.

Payroll is paid "up to the number of business days shown on the Schedule," but "business days" is undefined and the business income definition (c213) already turns on whether charges "necessarily continue." How the ninety-day payroll cap interacts with that definition is unresolved.

The definition excepts officers, executives, managers and contract employees, then continues "and Payroll expense includes" a list of the very components just excepted, so the sentence contradicts itself grammatically. What payroll is covered cannot be read off the clause.

The endorsement's deductibles apply only "If G. 2. or G. 3. d. on Form RM1000 is marked with an (X)," but the Declarations items bearing those marks are printed with their captions detached from their amounts (c021, c023). Whether the condition to this endorsement's operation is satisfied cannot be verified within the instrument.

The largest-deductible rule is qualified by paragraph C. (c316), which makes asterisked amounts separate and additive, and by the Named Storm provision (c317), which builds a single deductible by adding factors. Whether deductibles combine in a given loss depends on these against each other.

The Named Storm deductible is built by "adding up" percentage and flat factors "listed in Paragraph C.," but paragraph C. (c319) lists factors only for first and second tier wind counties, none of which is in Kansas. Whether any Named Storm deductible applies to these Wichita locations is left unanswered.

The only deductible categories are first and second tier wind Counties and Parishes, defined in DEFINITIONS N. and L.L. (c223, c247) to include no Kansas county, so the table supplies no factor for any insured location. The tie-breaker for a location falling in "two or more of the following categories" is likewise inoperable.

The press deductibles are graded by tonnage bands whose boundaries are stated only as "250 to 1,000 tons", "1,001 to 3,000" and so on, with no rule for presses below 250 tons. Equipment outside the bands has no stated deductible.

The waiting period is stated as "Not Applicable hours," so the condition on which loss of business income and perishable goods coverage depends has no number. Whether that means no waiting period or an unsatisfiable one is left open.

The item is unmarked yet states the sublimit "is increased from $25,000 to $Not Applicable," so it is unclear whether the arson reward remains $25,000 or is eliminated. The same construction is repeated throughout this endorsement.
The unmarked item states an increase "from $25,000 to $Not Applicable," leaving unclear whether the computer virus sublimit stands or is removed. The box and the text point in different directions.

The unmarked item states an increase "from $25,000 to $Not Applicable" for deferred payments, so whether the original sublimit survives is uncertain. The form gives no rule for unmarked amendments carrying text.

The item's marking box is corrupted and it states the fine arts sublimit "is increased from $100,000 to $Not Applicable," leaving the operative sublimit uncertain. Whether the amendment took effect cannot be told from the text.

The item states the fungus cleanup sublimit "is increased from $250,000 to $Not Applicable" with its selection box corrupted, so whether the $250,000 in EXTENSIONS A. 10. b. survives is unclear. The text and the marking cannot both be given effect.

The installation sublimit is said to be "increased from $250,000 to $Not Applicable" with a corrupted selection box, so the operative sublimit is indeterminate. The provision states a change without a figure.
The lock and key sublimit is said to be "increased from $25,000 to $Not Applicable" and the selection box is missing entirely from the text. Whether any amendment applies cannot be determined.
The plants, trees or shrubs sublimit is said to be "increased from $100,000 to $Not Applicable" with no legible selection box. The clause states an amendment whose amount is not a figure.

This deletes the ninety-day temporary-location period in EXTENSIONS A. 17. b. (1) (c083) and replaces it with "up to NA days," leaving no ascertainable period of coverage at a place of safekeeping. Whether removal coverage at the temporary location survives at all is the question.

This grants up to $100,000 for contract penalties although COVERAGES C. 8. b. (2) and D. 3. e. (2) (c035, c038) exclude "fines or damage for breach of contract for late or non-completion of orders, or for penalties of any nature." The endorsement states it modifies only C. 8. b. (2), leaving the parallel extra expense exclusion untouched.

Payment requires that the insured "be found to be legally liable" under a written contract, without saying by whom — a court, an arbitrator or the insurer — or whether a negotiated payment qualifies. The trigger is undefined while paragraph 3. denies any defense obligation.

The definition says the TRIA criteria "include the following" two items, an open-ended formulation that does not state the full test for a certified act. What else must be satisfied is left outside the policy.

This adds a terrorism exclusion as item 12 of GROUP A although the DECLARATIONS record the terrorism premium as "$Declined," so the relationship between the declination and the exclusion is stated in two places without being reconciled. Whether any terrorism coverage exists must be read across both.

The fire exception gives the full limit for property "in any and all States listed on the Schedule of this endorsement" and $1,000,000 elsewhere, and Kansas is not on the schedule. The result for these Kansas locations follows only from reading the exception against the state list.

The cap is measured over "a program year (January 1 through December 31)" while the TRIA disclosure form (c387) states the same cap by reference to a "calendar year." The two descriptions of the measuring period are not identical.

The insurer pays "the reasonable extra costs of temporary repair to property or of expediting the permanent repair or replacement of the property, whichever is less," so the insured cannot choose the more effective measure. Which costs are compared, and against what baseline, is not stated.

Payment otherwise "will be determined in accordance with the valuations endorsement," but the policy contains a VALUATIONS form (RM1005) and no valuations endorsement. The cross-reference points to a document not in the instrument.

"As used here, covered property does not include animals" narrows a policy-wide defined term for this coverage only, while PROPERTY NOT COVERED (c126) already excludes animals generally. The provision either duplicates or, by implication, qualifies that exclusion.

This pays up to $100,000 to "research, replace and restore lost data," while VALUATIONS C. 4. (c135) allows only the cost of transferring from backup and expressly refuses to pay research costs. The two state opposite rules for the same expense.

Water damage resulting from an accident to an object is covered here, while GROUP A exclusion 3. (c103) excludes flood, which is defined to include surface water and rain accumulation. Which governs water escaping from equipment during a storm requires reading the two together.

"Any substance that is hazardous to health or has been declared to be hazardous to health by a governmental agency" states no threshold of hazard and no identified agency. Almost any contaminant could satisfy the first limb.

This deletes and replaces COVERAGES D. 2. (c037), substituting thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit for the twenty-one days printed in the form. Both texts are delivered, and which applies to a civil-authority extra expense claim depends on giving the endorsement effect.

This deletes and replaces COVERAGES C. 3. (c031), substituting thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit for the twenty-one days in the printed form. The delivered policy contains both provisions on the same subject.

This deletes and replaces COVERAGES C. 4. (c031), substituting thirty days and a $1,000,000 limit for the twenty-one days in the printed form. Which text governs an ingress/egress business income claim depends on the endorsement's effect.

This adds an extra expense ingress/egress extension, a coverage COVERAGES D. (c037) never granted, so it operates as a new grant rather than a replacement while the parallel business income provision was amended by deletion. Whether the extra expense exclusions in D. 3. apply to this new grant is left unaddressed.

The endorsement "applies only to covered property located in Kansas," so its appraisal, fraud and suit changes govern some property and not others under a single policy with a nationwide territory clause (c182). How the conditions operate on a claim spanning states is not addressed.

This makes appraisal available only "if both parties agree, voluntarily," replacing the unilateral demand right in CONDITIONS B. 1. (c139) and changing the notice period from thirty to sixty days. Both texts remain in the delivered policy, and whether appraisal can be compelled turns on which applies.

The final sentence is truncated — "An appraisa p i" — so the provision's statement about the effect of an appraisal award is missing. Whether an award binds the parties cannot be determined from the words delivered.

This denies only "any loss or damage caused by or resulting from" a fraudulent insurance act and requires restitution, whereas CONDITIONS I. (c156) voids the entire policy for fraud. The consequence of insured misrepresentation is stated two different ways in the same instrument.

A fraudulent insurance act requires "written statements where the known intent is to defraud," a formulation that excludes oral misstatements and leaves "known intent" undefined. Whose knowledge and what proof suffices is not stated.

This replaces CONDITIONS Y. (c190) with a five-year limitation running from "the date on which the physical damage occurred," while the form it replaces prescribes two years. Both texts are in the delivered policy and only one can bar a suit.
This substitutes a ninety-day new-policy window for the sixty-day window in CONDITIONS F. 2. (c147). The two provisions state different periods for the same cancellation right.

This substitutes a different list of cancellation grounds and notice periods for CONDITIONS F. 3. (c148), including sixty days for grounds the form allowed on ten days' notice. Which list governs a Kansas cancellation is settled only by giving the endorsement effect.

The disclosure says the terrorism premium "is shown on the DECLARATIONS" if purchased, while the Declarations show that premium as "$Declined" and the EXCLUSION OF CERTIFIED ACT(S) OF TERRORISM endorsement excludes the peril. Whether any terrorism coverage was purchased has to be read across the three.

This states the $100 billion cap by reference to a "calendar year" while the terrorism exclusion endorsement (c353) states it by reference to "a program year (January 1 through December 31)." The two descriptions of the same statutory cap are not stated identically.
